agent_verdicts.reason: Mypy correctly infers the type of the concatenated list `starts + stops` as `list[Union[Literal['start'], Literal['stop']]]`. When two lists `list[T1]` and `list[T2]` are concatenated using the `+` operator, the operation creates a new list. The elements of this new list can originate from either the first list (typed `T1`) or the second list (typed `T2`). Therefore, the most appropriate type for the elements of the resulting list is the union of the two element types, i.e., `Union[T1, T2]`. In this specific case, `list[Literal['start']] + list[Literal['stop']]` should result in `list[Union[Literal['start'], Literal['stop']]]`. Mypy's type inference aligns with this expectation, and since the explicit annotation for `all_events` (`list[Union[Literal['start'], Literal['stop']]]`) matches the inferred type, no errors are reported.
